name: Nasal valve repair

card.summary: Functional surgery to widen or support the narrowest part of the nasal airway when it collapses; the literature is mostly case series with improvements reported.
card.note: A breathing operation first; appearance changes can accompany it.

quick.overview:
The nasal valve is the narrowest part of the nasal airway. When its walls are weak or narrow, the nostrils can collapse inward on inhalation. Nasal valve repair covers surgical ways of supporting or widening it, often with cartilage grafts or sutures.

It appears in looksmaxxing discussion mainly as a breathing fix that overlaps with nose shaping.
quick.mechanism: Surgeons typically add structural support, for example spreader or batten-type grafts, or use minimally invasive implants, sometimes alongside septoplasty and turbinate surgery. Diagnosis often involves the Cottle manoeuvre, though its accuracy has been questioned.
quick.risks: A 25-year systematic review found supportive evidence for valve surgery but limited by study quality. Complications are those of nasal surgery in general, including persisting obstruction and the possibility of revision.

lead: Nasal valve repair refers to surgical techniques that treat obstruction caused by compromise of the nasal valve, the narrow region of the airway at the junction of the upper lateral cartilage, septum and turbinate. It is a form of functional rhinoplasty.[1][2]

A 25-year systematic review of the English-language literature examined the evidence for modern techniques and concluded on the basis of the studies it found that the topic had supporting data, with limits in study design.[1] A retrospective series of 53 consecutive patients assessed causes, efficacy and cosmetic effect of reconstruction.[2]
The sources reviewed contain no looksmaxxing forum discussion of this procedure, so community views are not documented here.
infobox: Cartilage grafting, sutures, minimally invasive implants

paras: A general rhinoplasty reference describes the internal valve as bounded by the upper lateral cartilage, septum, nasal floor and the head of the inferior turbinate, and the external valve as depending on the lower lateral cartilage. A valve angle above roughly 15 degrees is described as generally needed for unobstructed breathing.[3]

The Cottle manoeuvre, in which the cheek is pulled laterally during inspiration, is used to test for valve collapse. A 2020 study evaluated its validity and specificity, and the general reference notes false positives can occur.[4][3]
Overviews discuss diagnosis and treatment and innovations in nasal valve surgery.[5][6]

Reports describe grafts to widen or support the valve, and a minimally invasive repair evaluated with the NOSE scale.[7] A computational fluid dynamics study modelled the effect of individual components of septoplasty, turbinate reduction and nasal valve repair in one patient.[8] A study of an ultrasonic bone aspirator for turbinoplasty is part of the related airway literature.[9] A paper on persistent obstruction describes the structural contribution of the upper airway nasal complex.[10]
A meta-analysis examined whether antibiotic prophylaxis after rhinoplasty is associated with fewer complications.[11]

Human data consist of a 25-year systematic review of functional rhinoplasty and nasal valve repair, a retrospective series of 53 patients, a minimally invasive repair evaluated with the NOSE scale, and a single-patient computational model.[1][2][7][8] No randomised comparison appears in the sources reviewed.
